name: Giddalti
overview: Giddalti was a male Levite who served in a special role among the musicians and prophets of ancient Israel. As the son of Heman, he was set apart to prophesy using musical instruments such as lyres, harps, and cymbals. He was notably chosen as the twenty-second leader by lot among the singers, highlighting his recognized position within the Levitical musical ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Giddalti means 'I pronounce [G-d as] Great; I reared up,' reflecting a declaration of God's greatness and possibly a role in spiritual edification. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:4 and does not indicate that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Giddalti as the son of Heman, a notable figure connected with Levitical service. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are recorded in the biblical text regarding Giddalti.
scriptureSignificance: Giddalti's significance lies in his role within the Levitical musicians who were dedicated to prophesying through music, a ministry that contributed to the worship and spiritual life of Israel. Being chosen by lot as the twenty-second among the singers underscores his recognized service and God's sovereign ordering in the ministry of temple music. His involvement exemplifies the integration of musical artistry and prophetic ministry in honoring God.
